title: M/s Raghu Prime Metal Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sheo Kumar Singh, J.; Sudhir Kumar Saxena, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; bills henceforth as per Supply Code cycle if no payment default.
headnote: On a complaint that a distribution licensee had issued bills contrary to the billing cycle in the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the High Court, without examining the Nigam’s explanation that the cycle was changed for fear the industrial consumer would abscond, directed that bills would henceforth follow the Code cycle provided the consumer did not default in payment.
facts: The petitioner, M/s Raghu Prime Metal Pvt. Ltd., an industrial consumer, approached the Allahabad High Court complaining that electricity bills issued by Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. did not follow the billing cycle in the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Counsel for the Nigam appeared and conceded that the cycle had been changed because of an apprehension that the petitioner unit would run away. The Court heard both sides.

holding_units.holding: Without going into merits, the Court directed the licensee henceforth to issue bills as per the billing cycle in the Electricity Supply Code, provided the consumer makes no default in payment.
holding_units.flag: order cites the Supply Code billing cycle without a numbered clause

not_decided.point: Whether the licensee could lawfully alter the billing cycle on an apprehension that the consumer unit would run away
not_decided.note: Court expressly declined to go into the merits.
